notes: The source test builds a real .mrpack (ZIP) file via a Python3 subprocess so it can control the stored Unix permission bits precisely (zipfile.ZipInfo.external_attr). 'archive.entries[].unixMode' is that stored POSIX mode string, distinct from whatever mode the file ends up with after extraction to disk. The manifest entry is stored with Unix mode 000 (unreadable by anyone). /usr/bin/unzip would extract this verbatim as an unreadable file on disk (mode 000 preserved) and MSC 1 would then fail to read it; MSC 1 instead extracts via macOS's `ditto` utility, which yields a readable file regardless — this was the root fix for a real-world BMC4 modpack import failure. IMPORTANT for the Rust port: `ditto` is a macOS-only tool. Whatever extraction approach Rust uses (a zip crate, or shelling out) needs to independently guarantee readability regardless of a stored-entry's permission bits — this fixture's behavior, not `ditto` itself, is what must be preserved.
